findings.issue: The only saved snapshot for the sole case (REVIEW_SOURCES.json → data/collections/sources/20a5b602287f558ec8e8bc291adcada932c33daab20662c4f2daf1fc58aaeed2.txt) is a JavaScript-rendered Google Sites shell: it contains page scripts, styling, and an <meta> description, but no product body copy. The only substantive text is "Co$tingNatureMAP - a simple visualisation and analysis tool for global Co$tingNature data, open access here", plus two lines describing global and local dashboards for national-scale nature/poverty metrics and hyper-resolution site-scale use. Nothing in the snapshot states 18 ecosystem services, supply/demand baselines, policy or land/climate scenario comparison, natural capital accounting, beneficiary analysis, or conservation/investment priority outputs. Yet batch.json's summary and leaf_matches reason assert all of these. The defining core (asset stock → quantified services → evaluated change → decision outputs) is therefore not evidenced by the cited body text, only by metadata and the entry's own prose.
findings.fix: Replace or supplement the source with a snapshot of Co$tingNature documentation/overview text (e.g. a product description, user guide, or methodology page on policysupport.org) that actually states which ecosystem services are quantified, how baseline vs scenario change is computed, and what outputs are produced; re-derive the summary from that text. If no such text can be captured, record the gap and remove the case rather than keeping claims derived only from the page shell/metadata.

findings.issue: Service-form and commercial facts asserted in the entry and research record are not supported by the snapshot and partly conflict with it: the snapshot advertises the tools as "open access", while the entry claims a hosted service requiring user registration, a free non-commercial account, and tiered licensing. The attribution to King's College London, AmbioTEK and UNEP-WCMC also appears nowhere in the captured text. With the core workflow unproven and the delivered form described as an "open access" visualisation/dashboard tool, the 'commercial' track and 'complete continuous web service' classification currently rest on assertion alone.
findings.fix: Capture a page that documents access model (registration/account, free non-commercial tier, paid/tiered licence) and the developing organizations, and cite it for those statements; if the product is in fact open-access visualisation without accounts/tiers, correct the summary, track justification, and leaf_matches reason (including whether it is a full application service or only a data viewer).
